Another round of heavy rains and flash flooding has triggered evacuations along rivers and parts

Portions of the areas affected are among the most remote in the continental U.S.,

There's hope for at least some people suffering from long COVID that the syndrome may get better
with time, and PR's Rob Stein has the story. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital
in Boston followed more than 1,000 adults suffering from long COVID. In the annals of
internal medicine, the researchers report that after two years, more than a third of the patients
symptoms had improved. After three years, more than half had gotten better, and nearly 27 percent
had experienced a complete remission. The researchers say the results indicate that
recovery is possible for many long COVID patients, but that new treatments are still
urgently needed for those who are still debilitated by the syndrome. Rob Stein, NPR News.
A new dinosaur dig site near Arches National Park in Utah could be one of the oldest Cretaceous
bone beds in North America. According to KSL, fossils found at the site outside of Moab could
date back 138 to 141 million years. They also believe the site could contain a new dinosaur
species. Scientists hope the discovery will help them better understand a mass
extinction that happened during the transition from the Jurassic to the Cretaceous period.
